verses.1: Israel is entangled in deceit, Ephraim in deception, and Judah has stubbornly persisted with God and with the holy ones, still remaining faithful.
verses.2: Ephraim is a restless spirit, a greedy pursuer all day long, multiplying falsehood and theft, and making a covenant with Assyria, sending oil to Egypt.
verses.3: Yet a dispute belongs to the LORD with Judah, to call to account Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
verses.4: In the womb he struck his brother and in his strength he contended with God.
verses.5: He wrestled with the angel and prevailed. He wept and sought my favor at Bethel, and there he spoke with me.
verses.6: The LORD, the God of Hosts, will be his remembrance.
verses.7: And you—return to your God, hold fast to love and justice, and wait continually for your God.
verses.8: Like Canaan in his hand—false scales to oppress the beloved.
verses.9: And Ephraim said, “I have grown wealthy; I have found peace for myself.” But all his toil will not find him innocence, for his sins remain.
verses.10: Yet I am the LORD your God, from the land of Egypt I will again settle you in tents, as in the days of a festival.
verses.11: I will speak to the prophets, and I myself have multiplied visions, and by the hands of the prophets I have been compared.
verses.12: If Gilgal is iniquity, surely the Gilgalites have been false. Their bulls are sacrificed, and their altars are like heaps in a field.
verses.13: Jacob fled to the field of Aram, and Israel served in a woman, and in a woman he guarded.
verses.14: The LORD brought Israel up from Egypt by a prophet, and by a prophet he was preserved.
verses.15: Ephraim provokes bitter wrath, and his blood will be on himself. His disgrace the Lord will repay to him, his master.

notes:
Notes
- v. 9: "I have found peace for myself" reflects the Hebrew "מָצָאתִי אוֹן לִי" which can be read as "I have found a yoke for myself" or "I have found rest for myself." The latter is chosen here to reflect Ephraim's false sense of security.
- v. 12: "Gilgal" is used both as a location and as a metaphor for Israel's covenant renewal. The phrase "If Gilgal is iniquity" reflects this dual usage.
- v. 14: "by a prophet" (בְּנָבִיא) is rendered in parallel with v. 11 and reflects the LORD's guidance through human instruments.

[1] Israel is entangled in deceit, Ephraim in deception, and Judah has stubbornly persisted with God and with the holy ones, still remaining faithful.

[2] Ephraim is a restless spirit, a greedy pursuer all day long, multiplying falsehood and theft, and making a covenant with Assyria, sending oil to Egypt.

[3] Yet a dispute belongs to the LORD with Judah, to call to account Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.

[4] In the womb he struck his brother and in his strength he contended with God.

[5] He wrestled with the angel and prevailed. He wept and sought my favor at Bethel, and there he spoke with me.

[6] The LORD, the God of Hosts, will be his remembrance.

[7] And you—return to your God, hold fast to love and justice, and wait continually for your God.

[8] Like Canaan in his hand—false scales to oppress the beloved.

[9] And Ephraim said, “I have grown wealthy; I have found peace for myself.” But all his toil will not find him innocence, for his sins remain.

[10] Yet I am the LORD your God, from the land of Egypt I will again settle you in tents, as in the days of a festival.

[11] I will speak to the prophets, and I myself have multiplied visions, and by the hands of the prophets I have been compared.

[12] If Gilgal is iniquity, surely the Gilgalites have been false. Their bulls are sacrificed, and their altars are like heaps in a field.

[13] Jacob fled to the field of Aram, and Israel served in a woman, and in a woman he guarded.

[14] The LORD brought Israel up from Egypt by a prophet, and by a prophet he was preserved.

[15] Ephraim provokes bitter wrath, and his blood will be on himself. His disgrace the Lord will repay to him, his master.
